content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge decides an UNDERDETERMINED result for the Matthew 1:16 link by assessing whether the verse itself and the other text's own words state a contrary verdict, rather than weighing the pressed chain against the defender's chain by footing.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"The phrase 'neither text's own words' versus K-C's 'never verse by verse': (A) the absence of a single verse stating the contrary cannot decide the link, or (B) it may be used only if not deciding by chain-against-chain footing; the judge used it to decide UNDERDETERMINED, so A applies.","why":"K-C retires the stating-verse test, so the judge cannot leave the link UNDERDETERMINED on the ground that neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary."}
